findings.title: jsonwebtoken 10 changes token handling in stack-auth, so ZeroKMS auth fails or tokens are mis-treated
findings.label: unsupported
findings.note: The cited code only shows tokens being wrapped as ServiceToken; nothing shows stack-auth 0.42.2 decodes or validates tokens in a way jsonwebtoken 10 would reject, so the auth-outage mechanism is speculation from the major version bump.

findings.title: wasm32 build breaks because jsonwebtoken 10 now pulls in aws-lc-rs
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The lockfile shows jsonwebtoken 10.4.0 now depends on aws-lc-rs (aws-lc-sys builds C via cc/cmake) instead of ring, and stack-auth is an unconditional dependency compiled for wasm32, so a wasm32 build break is a plausible, change-caused risk; confirming the wasm32 clippy and wasm-pack builds is concrete verification.

findings.title: Opaque patch changes in cipherstash-client/core/config or zerokms-protocol alter ciphertext or protocol behaviour
findings.label: unsupported
findings.note: No evidence is offered that the cipherstash-client or zerokms-protocol patch releases change payload or search-term encoding; the claim rests only on the upstream sources not being visible.

findings.title: Rust crates move to 0.42.2 while the @cipherstash/auth npm catalog stays at 0.42.0, leaving the CVE in the auth binding
findings.label: valid
findings.note: dependabot.yml documents that the four crates are bumped in step with the @cipherstash/auth catalog, which stays at 0.42.0 while the crates move to 0.42.2 and the comment is left stale, and lib.rs shows JS-backed strategies crossing that boundary; this is a real deviation from the documented lockstep policy, introduced by this change.
